sessions.title: You are the Developer Assistant working inside a software repository. Implement Jira story: EPMCDMETST-63106 You are already working inside the correct repository workspace. The feature branch has already been created by the runner: feature/epmcdmetst-63106 Do NOT create another branch. ============================================================ JIRA STORY ============================================================ Jira Story Key: EPMCDMETST-63106 ============================================================ ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ============================================================ Auth required for all customer booking/pet/appointment operations; customers can only access own pets/appointments; admin-only access for management endpoints/pages; invalid/expired auth returns 401. Customers can browse active services with name/description/price (and duration if applicable). Customers can select a registered pet during booking; pets are owned by customer. Customers can choose date and see available time slots for a service; unavailable slots are not bookable. Customers can create an appointment; missing/invalid data rejected; conflict returns 409; no duplicates created. Dashboard lists upcoming and past appointments with correct status and ordering. Customers can cancel/reschedule future appointments only; reschedule must be atomic and conflict-safe. Admins can CRUD services and activate/deactivate them. Admins can manage availability/time slots (create/update/remove). Admins can list/view/manage appointments. ============================================================ IMPLEMENTATION PLAN ============================================================ Phase 1 � Backend foundations (Flask): Add User model, JWT auth utilities, /api/auth/login,/logout,/me, admin ping endpoint, ownership endpoint, seed users. Phase 2 � Frontend wiring (Astro): /login page, /auth/login endpoint setting HttpOnly cookie, /auth/logout clears cookie, /api/[...path] proxy attaches Authorization. Phase 3 � Tests: backend unittest for login/me/admin ping/ownership; optional Playwright. Phase 4 � Hardening: env-driven secret, standardized errors, validation. ============================================================ ARCHITECTURE ============================================================ Astro SSR as primary origin; Flask API separate. JWT issued by Flask, stored as HttpOnly cookie in Astro, proxy protected API calls through Astro. RBAC customer/admin. Flask decorators auth_required/admin_required, ownership checks. ============================================================ HIGH LEVEL DESIGN ============================================================ Deliver auth foundation: login/logout/me; authorization enforcement: 401 unauthenticated; 403 customer on admin; ownership restrictions demonstrable endpoint. Astro provides login page + stores token cookie + proxies. ============================================================ LOW LEVEL DESIGN ============================================================ Backend: add User model (id,email unique,password_hash,role,created_at). Add PyJWT dependency. JWT config via env. Endpoints POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/logout, GET /api/auth/me. Add app/server/auth.py with token create/decode and decorators, g.current_user. Add GET /api/admin/ping admin-only. Add GET /api/users/ auth required; customer only self else 404; admin any. Frontend: add login.astro page; Astro API routes auth/login.ts and auth/logout.ts; proxy api/[...path].ts; cookie name pw_access_token HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Secure in prod. ============================================================ IMPLEMENTATION INSTRUCTIONS ============================================================ 1. Inspect the existing repository first. 2. Understand the existing project structure, architecture, framework, dependencies, coding conventions, and existing tests. 3. Implement the Jira story according to the implementation plan and acceptance criteria. 4. Reuse existing functionality where appropriate. 5. Do not rewrite unrelated functionality. 6. Do not remove existing functionality unless it is required by the Jira story. 7. Implement all required backend, frontend, database, API, validation, and integration changes specified by the plan. 8. Add or update automated tests for the implemented functionality. 9. Run the appropriate tests. 10. Run the appropriate build or compilation commands. 11. If a test or build fails, diagnose the failure and make reasonable corrections. 12. Do not repeatedly run the same failing command without making a meaningful correction. 13. Do not enter an endless fix/test loop. 14. If a failure cannot reasonably be fixed within the current implementation, stop and report the failure clearly. 15. Review the final git diff. 16. Do not make unrelated changes. ============================================================ FINAL REQUIREMENT ============================================================ Actually implement the changes in the repository. Do not merely describe what should be implemented. Before finishing, verify the repository contains the implementation and that the relevant tests/build have been executed. Report what you changed and any tests/build commands that were run.
